title: Hotfix: Backport host/origin validation to requests and websocket connections
body:
## What I did

This is a backport of #33835 for Storybook v7.6.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Host validation for HTTP and WebSocket connections with origin and token checks.
  * New allowedHosts configuration; shown in startup logs (lists hosts or "all (insecure)").
  * Server considers local and network addresses when validating connections and returns 403 for invalid hosts/origins.
  * Runtime warning when binding to 0.0.0.0 without allowedHosts configured.

* **Tests**
  * Expanded tests covering host/origin and token validation scenarios.

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Use second-pass `core.allowedHosts` for warning and startup output.**

`allowedHosts` is captured at Line 104 before presets are rebuilt, then reused at Line 223 after the second pass. If later presets change `core.allowedHosts`, logs can be inaccurate and hide (or falsely report) insecure host behavior.



<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-  const { allowedHosts, renderer, builder, disableTelemetry } = await presets.apply('core', {});
+  const { renderer, builder, disableTelemetry } = await presets.apply('core', {});
...
-  // '0.0.0.0' binds to all interfaces, which is useful for Docker and other containerized environments.
-  // By default we allow requests from all hosts in this case, but the user should be made aware of the risk.
-  if (
-    options.host === '0.0.0.0' &&
-    (!allowedHosts || (allowedHosts !== true && allowedHosts.length === 0))
-  ) {
-    logger.warn(dedent`
-      --host is set to 0.0.0.0 but no allowedHosts are defined. Allowing all hosts.
-      To restrict allowed hosts, set core.allowedHosts in your main Storybook config.
-      See: https://storybook.js.org/docs/api/main-config/main-config-core
-    `);
-  }
...
   presets = await loadAllPresets({
     corePresets: [
       require.resolve('@storybook/core-server/dist/presets/common-preset'),
       ...(managerBuilder.corePresets || []),
       ...(previewBuilder.corePresets || []),
       ...(resolvedRenderer ? [resolvedRenderer] : []),
       ...corePresets,
       require.resolve('@storybook/core-server/dist/presets/babel-cache-preset'),
     ],
     overridePresets: [
       ...(previewBuilder.overridePresets || []),
       require.resolve('@storybook/core-server/dist/presets/common-override-preset'),
     ],
     ...options,
   });

+  const { allowedHosts } = await presets.apply('core', {});
+
+  // '0.0.0.0' binds to all interfaces, which is useful for Docker and other containerized environments.
+  // By default we allow requests from all hosts in this case, but the user should be made aware of the risk.
+  if (
+    options.host === '0.0.0.0' &&
+    (!allowedHosts || (allowedHosts !== true && allowedHosts.length === 0))
+  ) {
+    logger.warn(dedent`
+      --host is set to 0.0.0.0 but no allowedHosts are defined. Allowing all hosts.
+      To restrict allowed hosts, set core.allowedHosts in your main Storybook config.
+      See: https://storybook.js.org/docs/api/main-config/main-config-core
+    `);
+  }
```
</details>


Also applies to: 223-223

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```

In `@code/lib/core-server/src/build-dev.ts` around lines 104 - 117, The warning
uses the stale allowedHosts value captured from the first presets.apply('core',
{}) call; update the code to re-read core.allowedHosts from
presets.apply('core', {}) (or from the second-pass presets where core is
finalized) immediately before emitting the logger.warn and any startup output so
the check uses the final allowedHosts value; locate the allowedHosts variable
and the logger.warn block and replace its condition to reference the freshly
obtained allowedHosts (or a helper like resolveAllowedHosts()) used later at
startup to ensure accurate warnings about --host 0.0.0.0.
```

</details>

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Remove the implicit allow-all path for `0.0.0.0`.**

Line 37 bypasses validation entirely when `allowedHosts` is empty, which weakens this host-validation hotfix and permits arbitrary Host headers.



<details>
<summary>Suggested change</summary>

```diff
-    // Setting host to 0.0.0.0 binds to all hosts, which implies allowing all hosts.
-    // This is common in containerized environments like Docker.
-    if (options.host === '0.0.0.0' && allowedHosts.length === 0) {
-      return true;
-    }
+    // Keep host validation active even when binding to 0.0.0.0.
+    // If callers truly want to disable checks, they can set allowedHosts: true explicitly.
```
</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
    // Keep host validation active even when binding to 0.0.0.0.
    // If callers truly want to disable checks, they can set allowedHosts: true explicitly.
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/lib/core-server/src/utils/getHostValidationMiddleware.ts` around lines
35 - 39, The current early-return in getHostValidationMiddleware that treats
options.host === '0.0.0.0' and allowedHosts.length === 0 as valid must be
removed; instead, do not bypass host validation for 0.0.0.0—either remove that
conditional entirely or change the logic to only allow all hosts when an
explicit wildcard entry (e.g., '*' or a documented allow-all marker) exists in
allowedHosts; update the validation flow around options.host and the
allowedHosts check so Host headers are always validated unless explicitly
configured to allow all.
```

</details>

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Correct the Host-header behavior note in docs.**

Line 52 is misleading: browser address-bar/same-origin HTTP/1.1 requests normally include a `Host` header. The current wording may confuse future maintainers.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/lib/core-server/src/utils/getHostValidationMiddleware.ts` around lines
51 - 53, Update the misleading comment in getHostValidationMiddleware: change
the sentence that claims "Requests with no Host header (e.g. same-origin
navigation, GET from address bar) are not allowed" to accurately state that
modern browsers and address-bar navigations normally include a Host header
(HTTP/1.1+), and clarify that missing Host headers occur only for
older/non-HTTP/1.1 clients or malformed requests; ensure this revised note
appears alongside the getHostValidationMiddleware validation description so
future maintainers are not confused.
```

</details>

**Avoid `as any` on shared transport options.**

The `as any` cast bypasses TypeScript strict mode and can hide option-shape regressions when `ServerChannelTransportOptions` evolves. Use the constructor parameter type directly:

<details>

```diff

+const options: ConstructorParameters<typeof ServerChannelTransport>[1] = {
   localAddress: 'http://localhost:6006',
   networkAddress: 'http://192.168.1.100:6006',
   token: mockToken,
-} as any;
+};
```
</details>
